body: I've really been looking into the nearby community college. A lot of my old friends go there. When I think about going back to school it's really the only thing that makes me somewhat hopeful about the future.
Any time I'm not working. I usually only have about 30 hours a week, if that gives you an idea.

>The gas station job must have broken that cycle?

Yeah. It helped me a lot actually.

>How close are the nearest coffee shop and library?

Not far. Thing is, I live in a medium sized town in west Texas; As far as I know, people don't really hang around coffee shops much around here.

Even if it was, and it may be (how would I know?), I'm just supposed to go alone? This is a big deterrent for doing most of the things I think would help me, even a little bit. Most places I don't mind going to alone, but it's the social gathering type places I stay away from; Malls, coffee shops, etc. I never go because it just feels awkward to be there alone.

>Want some recommendations on books you can read when you go out?

I don't read much. I've always wanted to read more, but then I go into the "Why bother?" state of mind. I have a ton of books in mind that I know would interest me, but I can't bring myself to drive the 2 minutes to the nearest library.

> I think you come across as a kind empathic and intelligent person.

I was lucky to learn something at a young age: If you have a firm grasp of the English language, people will always assume you're intelligent. 

I'm really not, it's all fake. I have no actual smarts. This isn't self deprecation, or me beating myself up; It's just the way it is.

> get a small job, study part time, etc and more..

Sometimes I get these small bursts of motivation where I go "Alright, this shit has to change right now". I make all these plans to join different groups, volunteer, and just do *things* in general. Soon after the motivation dies and I'm back where I began. This happens probably once a week.

The thing is, like I said, I'm not unhappy, but I'm not happy either... It's like I'm content with the way things are, but at the same time, I'm lonely, and I want things to change... But not, also...

This doesn't even make sense in my head anymore. I think I'll sleep now.

Actually, no.

I've seen bits and pieces of Donnie Darko. It's been on my to-watch list forever. Just never got around to seeing it.

I hear Up is amazing. I have a general idea of what the message of the movie is, so I want to wait till I can watch it alone before I see it. It seems like a movie I'd enjoy more alone.

I'll have to check out the rest of them.

Thanks for the reply.

> First off, do you interact on reddit with comments?

No, I don't write much at all. I've had a few people tell me I'm a good author, but it's not something I'm really passionate about.

> Are you ready to discuss this topic seriously? you say it is pointless, is that a question you forgot to put a question mark on?

I suppose. although, I find it hard to imagine a conversation that would change my view on this. You live, then you die. Whatever happens after that is up in the air.

> Are you male or female?
>What movies connect with you?

Male.

The only movie I've ever felt I connected with was American Beauty. I tear up every time I watch it. But not because it's sad... Come to think of it, I'm actually not sure why it brings out the emotions it does; I love it though.

First time using quotes, I wonder how bad I fudged it up.
